selected.look_here_first: Begin with a grasslike basal rosette and upright flowering stalk; look closely at the clustered small yellow tubular flowers and their six lobes.
Look for leafless orange twining threads around a host; magnify flower clusters and calyx/corolla lobes to separate other Cuscuta.
Find the parasitic yellow-orange threads and small clustered flowers; inspect the calyx, rounded floral lobes and developing seed capsules.
Inspect triangular stems, the terminal umbrella of flattened spikelets and their leaflike bracts; check mature achenes.
Inspect the dense whitish wool on the low plant and its clustered inconspicuous flower heads; confirm the heads under magnification.
Look at the small woolly plant with tightly clustered composite heads; compare the branching head clusters and phyllaries with other Diaperia.
Find the tiny silvery hairy spring annual and its compact flower-head clusters; examine the bracts surrounding each head.
Start with the airy branching panicles; inspect leaf sheaths, ligules and tiny spikelets to distinguish other panicgrasses.
Look for tufted grass with a fairly open panicle and scattered spikelets; check basal leaf hairs, sheaths and individual glumes.
Check the dissected leaves, yellow composite flower heads and phyllaries; look closely at the disk florets and seed heads.
Recognize hairy stems and leaves and yellow daisy-like heads; inspect the layers of phyllaries and the hairy leaf surfaces.
Look for tiny free-floating green flattened fronds with one simple root each; compare with multi-rooted Spirodela and rootless Wolffia.
Look for a tall raceme of small flat rounded seedpods; inspect pod notches, flowers and different basal versus stem leaves.
Recognize the tuft of long narrow tough leaves; inspect leaf margins, flowering panicle and mature fruit.
Inspect the inconspicuous cyathia at the branch tips, gland shapes and developing three-lobed capsules; compare leaf arrangement with related spurges.
